description: Law schedules: EXAMPLE CONTENT, not a default (D18). A schedule says how a law whose substance is a few figures is written from them: the figures (their types and units), and the law's words, its Institutional Grammar breakdown and, where acts can be checked against it, its rule (a formal CEL condition), with {figure} standing for a figure as worded and {figure:unit} for the number as held. A world's opening laws are written from these with a place's figures (from its profile), and a council's clerk writes an amended law the same way, from the figures on the law's amendment form (docs/behaviour/government.md). A schedule holds no place's figures.

records.author: genesis
records.text: How the law on rent increases is written from its figures: the least time between increases, and the notice of one.

data.title: the law on rent increases

review.label: least time between increases
review.description: The least time between one increase of a tenancy's rent and the next.

notice.label: notice of an increase
notice.description: The least written notice a tenant must have of an increase.

data.text: A residential rent may be increased no more than once every {review}, and only on written notice to the tenant of at least {notice}. Or else: the increase is invalid.

adico.condition: more than once in {review}, or on written notice of less than {notice}

records.author: genesis
records.text: How the law on industrial action is written from its figures: the turnout and the majority a ballot needs, and the notice an employer must have.

data.title: the law on industrial action

turnout.label: turnout a ballot needs
turnout.description: The least share of the members concerned who must vote, in percent, as a whole number.

majority.label: share of the votes that must be exceeded
majority.description: The share of the votes cast that the yes votes must exceed, in percent, as a whole number.

notice.label: notice to the employer
notice.description: The least written notice the employer must have of the action.

data.text: Industrial action is protected only if a ballot of the members concerned approves it, with at least {turnout}% of them voting and more than {majority}% of the votes yes, and the employer has written notice of at least {notice}.

adico.condition: without an approving ballot ({turnout}% voting, more than {majority}% yes) and written notice of at least {notice}

data.formal: block.block == 'publish' && block.kind == 'industrial_action' && (block.data.from - now < {notice:seconds} || block.data.voted * 10000 < {turnout:basis_points} * block.data.eligible || block.data.yes * 10000 <= {majority:basis_points} * block.data.voted)

records.author: genesis
records.text: How the law on notice of industrial action is written from its figure, where no ballot is required: the notice an employer must have.

data.title: the law on notice of industrial action

notice.label: notice to the employer
notice.description: The least written notice the employer must have of the action.

data.text: Industrial action is protected only if the employer has written notice of at least {notice}.

adico.condition: without written notice to the employer of at least {notice}

records.author: genesis
records.text: How the law on ending a tenancy is written from its figures: the notice a landlord must give, and the notice a tenant may leave on.

data.title: the law on ending a tenancy

notice.label: a landlord's notice to end a tenancy
notice.description: The least written notice a landlord must give to end a tenancy.

tenant_notice.label: a tenant's notice to leave
tenant_notice.description: The notice a tenant may leave on.

data.text: A landlord may end a tenancy only by giving written notice of at least {notice}, and may not remove a tenant before the notice has run out. A tenant may leave on notice of {tenant_notice}. Or else: the removal is unlawful and the tenant may return.

adico.condition: before written notice of at least {notice} has run out
adico.or_else: the removal is unlawful; the tenant may return
